rules.name: Runs on Nebius Token Factory
rules.how: Every model call goes through Nebius Token Factory: MiniCPM-V reads, Nemotron Nano triages, Qwen3-Embedding retrieves, Nemotron Super reasons over any rule that has no deterministic formula. The application itself is deployed on self-hosted infrastructure; the rule is satisfied by Token Factory, which the rule names as an alternative to Nebius AI Cloud.

rules.name: ≥ 1 NVIDIA open-source model
rules.how: Three NVIDIA Nemotron models, all on Nebius Token Factory: Nemotron Nano triages each case, Nemotron Super reasons over rules without a deterministic formula and labels PDF form fields, and Nemotron 3 Nano 30B maps template fields at design time. Default enforced in tests: the Nebius provider's default model name must start with nvidia/.

architecture.one_liner: AI runs where it earns its place: reading documents, routing the case, finding the rules, and reasoning only where a rule needs judgment. Then AI stops. No language model sits on the code path that generates the audited artifact.

stages.why: Vision extraction over scanned, faxed and flat PDFs: enrollment forms, income worksheets, prescriptions. Each value lands in a typed field the rules can check.
A small, fast model classifies the case and picks its route. If it is unavailable a rule-based fallback takes over, so intake never blocks on a model.
Dense retrieval surfaces the program's human-authored rules that apply to this case. The model's job is to find, not to invent.

Reasons over any rule without a deterministic formula, in non-reasoning JSON mode. When every rule has a formula, as in the CardioVita demo, this stage is skipped and the verdict is composed from the rules alone.
The reply letter is merged from a frozen, human-approved template and held for a reviewer. Nothing is sent until a person approves.

reuse.principle: Hybrid: hackathon-window pipeline (Verdikt) composed onto a pre-existing doc-gen kernel (Quire). Mechanical boundaries make the split provable.

prior_work.scope: Design-time AI mapping, deterministic render path, freeze/publish, generic inbox agent, provider abstraction, multi-tenancy. Predates 2026-08-26.

One extension point on the inbox agent so Verdikt can plug in

judging_criteria.prompt: How well is the project built, and how effectively does it use Nebius Token Factory or AI Cloud model(s), and NVIDIA Nemotron as part of the solution?
points: Four models composed on Nebius Token Factory at their strongest task shapes, two of them NVIDIA: MiniCPM-V reads scanned intake, Nemotron Nano triages, Qwen3-Embedding retrieves the rules, and Nemotron Super reasons over any rule without a deterministic formula.
One Nebius key, one router, per-call instrumentation. Latency, cost, and cache-hit rate are visible on the admin routing page.
Nemotron stops at a hard boundary. Every artifact that leaves the pipeline (reply letter, JSON verdict) is written by deterministic Python from typed pydantic models.
A boundary test fails the build if an LLM ever leaks into the render path.
Audit-defensibility of a rules engine with the language quality of Nemotron.

judging_criteria.prompt: Does the project deliver a complete, coherent product experience not just a technical proof of concept?
points: Verdikt is a working product, not a notebook.
Fax, scanned paper, and portal submissions fan into a single email-normalized intake bus.
The pipeline emits a reply letter merged from a frozen, human-approved template and a structured JSON verdict a downstream call-center system can act on immediately.
Eight live dashboards (Overview, About, Features, Tests, Code, Security, Production, Hackathon) mirror what an operator actually needs, not just what a judge wants to see.

Prometheus /metrics ships per-tenant counters, latency histograms, queue-depth gauges, and preflight-rejection counters. An on-call can answer 'who is this load from, what's stuck, what's the P99' from one scrape.

judging_criteria.prompt: Does the project make a credible, specific case for solving a real problem for a real audience and does the solution actually address it based on what's demonstrated?
points: Patient Assistance Programs are one instance of a class: regulated document workflows where the letter that leaves the building is the audit artifact.
Prior authorization, benefit verification, informed consent, and MedWatch reporting all share the same shape and the same failure mode: humans transcribing forms all day, one keystroke from a denial.
The demo shows one program end-to-end, from a faxed application to a decisioned reply.
Onboarding a second program is a data change (rulebook plus templates), not a build.
A second use case reuses the pipeline unchanged; only the rulebook and templates are new.

judging_criteria.prompt: Is this a creative, non-obvious use of Nebius Token Factory or AI Cloud model(s), and NVIDIA Nemotron and does the team show genuine understanding of the problem space?
points: Most 2026 document-generation submissions put a language model directly on the artifact-generation code path. Verdikt refuses.
Models read, triage and rank on Nebius Token Factory; Nemotron reasons only where a rule needs judgment; deterministic code decides and writes.
The EU AI Act classifies healthcare eligibility decisions as high-risk and demands exactly the reproducibility guarantees Verdikt provides mechanically.
Using Nemotron for what it is uniquely good at (reasoning over messy healthcare policy) while keeping it off the artifact path is the non-obvious call.
The difference between a demo that impresses judges and a system that can be deployed on Monday.
